key: And I will be yet more vile than thus, and will be base in mine own sight; and with the handmaids whom thou hast spoken of, with them will I get me honour.
s: Rebuked by Michal, who scorns his dancing before the ark, David answers her; Radak, on 6:22, reads it as lowering himself before God, no disgrace but honour, since making light of himself for God’s honour makes him honoured in the eyes of all.

evidence.words: והייתי שפל בעיני. לפניו לכל דבר ואין זה קלון אלא כבוד … עמם אכבדה. בעיניהן אני נכבד במה שעשיתי כי אם אקל עצמי לכבוד האל אהיה נכבד בעיני הכל לא כמו בעיניך
evidence.gloss: ‘And will be base in mine own sight’: before Him in every matter, and this is no disgrace but honour … ‘With them will I get me honour’: in their eyes I am honoured by what I did, for if I make light of myself for the honour of God, I shall be honoured in the eyes of all, not as in yours.

reason: The problem holds: ‘Answering Michal ... David replies’ said the same thing twice. Context clause now ‘Rebuked by Michal, who scorns his dancing before the ark, David answers her’, which day.js supports (6:16 she despises him seeing him leaping and dancing before the LORD as the ark comes in; 6:20 her scornful words; 6:21 to 22 ‘And David said unto Michal’). No four-word run from the key. Reading, commentator, place and src unchanged.
